text:
emma: Heads-up — planning a rolling soft-reboot + NIC microcode patch for the apac-edge GPU pool tomorrow 04:00–08:00 UTC. This will be a staggered node drain (10-node cohorts), 5m drain each node, soft reboot BMC/NIC firmware, quick thermal + kernel sanity, then uncordon. Expected transient capacity hit ~25% during the busiest 30m; overall window ~4h. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/apac-edge-microcode.md. tagging @sre-oncall and @lia for customer comms.

raj: Ack. Two quick Qs — can we shift this to start at 04:00 instead of 03:00 (client traffic in AP spikes at 03:30)? Also what's fallback if backlog spikes (jobs queue)? Can we enable temporary burst backfill from eu pool?

sre-oncall: I'm available 04:00–06:00. We should enable backfill to eu for non-sensitive workloads, and throttle backfill for jobs tagged `enterprise:high-priority`. I'll prep a rapid rollback play: `ctl maintenance abort --id=MNT-2026-0456`.

jordan: Add a canary cohort (2 nodes) at t=00 for perf verification. Use `/tools/throughput-check --pool gpu-apac-edge --cohort canary` and gate on latency regressions >5% or 95th-p90 increase >20ms -> rollback. Also add post-step check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=gpu-apac-edge -o wide` to verify task rescheduling.

lia: I'll notify the top 3 AP enterprise tenants (INC contact list) and ask if they want maintenance blackout for their jobs. Ping CS with the customer list.

mike: Small ops note — please set pool autoscale bounds before window: `ctl pool set-autoscale --pool=gpu-apac-edge --min=3 --max=18`. That limits churn and avoids over-scheduling during backfill.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: MNT-2026-0456 — apac-edge NIC microcode + soft reboot — start 2026-04-12T04:00Z, duration 4h. Reminder set for 1h.

emma: Updated plan: start 04:00–08:00 UTC, canary at 04:00, 2 cohorts then ramp. Fallback: if backlog > 2x baseline for >15m we'll pause and start immediate backfill to eu with `route-policy=burst-backfill`. Cost note: backfill egress estimate ~ $1.5–2k for a 4h window.

raj: can you also annotate the maintenance with expected capacity numbers per cohort? helps capacity planning -> something like cohort A (10 nodes, -10%), cohort B (10 nodes, -10%), canary (2 nodes).

emma: Done. Cohort A: nodes 1–10 (-11% capacity), Cohort B: nodes 11–20 (-12%), Canary: nodes 21–22 (non-critical). Added to runbook.

deploy-bot: Canary cohort deployed at 04:00 UTC — health checks running (ps: 6/6). Latency delta: +0.8% (p95 +7ms). No anomalies in kernel logs so far.

sre-oncall: Saw the canary metrics, looks good. Proceeding to cohort A drain at +15m. I'll monitor queue length and notify if >200 pending jobs.

lia: CS notified customers. One tenant (AcmeGames) requested a heads-up 30m before we touch their hosts — I set `notify:30m` in the ticket.

mike: Reminder: after each cohort uncordon, run `ctl cache warmup --pool=gpu-apac-edge --prefix-cache` to reduce cold-start penalties.

emma: mid-window update: so far so good, no thermal spikes. Current capacity reduction steady at ~18%. Proceeding to cohort B.

ops-bot: Maintenance MNT-2026-0456 progress: Canary ✅, Cohort A ✅, Cohort B in progress. Estimated finish 07:10 UTC.

jordan: Quick retrospective note — we should add an automated metric gate next time to abort if p95 > baseline * 1.12. Filing a follow-up RFC.

emma: Thanks all. Postmortem and cost breakdown will be posted under MNT-2026-0456. If anyone saw unusual errors, paste logs here with `sha:` tag so we can attach. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Closing watch; leaving a 30m post-window observation.

deploy-bot: Maintenance MNT-2026-0456 completed at 07:08 UTC. All nodes healthy. Final reported cost impact: egress $1,850 (estimate).

emma: Archived. Good job team — no customer-facing incidents.
